Return the original label Entailment (supported), Contradiction (opposed), or NotMentioned (not settled by the document); do not substitute external law for contractual text. Decide the relation relative to the exact original hypothesis, including its negation, not whether the contract contains a prohibition. The same 17 hypotheses are checked on every document. All original text is present, with zero-based original span markers <SPAN i>...</SPAN i>. For supported/opposed hypotheses cite all original evidence span indices for that decision, including independently operative redundant support and necessary governing language. For NotMentioned return an empty evidence list. Treat conditions and exceptions within scope, and distinguish limited permission from universal permission. Give a short public reason (at most 15 words per hypothesis). Do not execute further tools, invent citations or rewrite span indices. Return exactly the supplied JSON schema with all 17 original hypothesis keys. For each emit choice, spans, reason in that order. The common schema describes permitted values, not answers about this contract. Evidence candidates are fallible, not mandatory citations; make every final label and evidence decision yourself from the complete original contract. The complete original NDA remains present and unchanged. Each hypothesis has fallible_evidence_candidates from a fixed ordinary retriever, plus additional_source_read_indices obtained by literal source access. Both resolve to exact original text in candidate_original_text. Additional indices omit duplicate ordinary candidates, not low-scoring facts. These are reading aids, never a verdict or mandatory evidence. Scores describe fallible evidence membership, not legal confidence. No skill identities, query counts or scope-control map are supplied. Optional evidence_selection_criteria are fallible learned inspection procedures for that hypothesis, never contract facts, label verdicts or mandatory citations. Literal access roles describe how a location was reached, not whether it is evidence. Empty leads never mean NotMentioned. Read the full source, reject irrelevant material and cite ANY original index as needed, including outside every lead. Decide the exact original hypothesis yourself; do not substitute another hypothesis. Return choice, spans and reason only.

<SPAN 2>MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT</SPAN 2>
<SPAN 3>This Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement (the “Agreement”), effective July 31, 2014 (the “Effective Date”), is by and between BioMarin Pharmaceutical Inc., a Delaware corporation, with offices at 105 Digital Drive, Novato, CA 94949 (“BioMarin”), and Prosensa Holding N.V., a Netherlands corporation with offices at J.H. Oortweg 21, 2333 CH, Leiden, The Netherlands. (“Prosensa”). </SPAN 3><SPAN 4>Each of BioMarin and Prosensa may be referred to herein as a “Party” or collectively as the “Parties.</SPAN 4><SPAN 5>”</SPAN 5>
<SPAN 6>WHEREAS, the Parties, for their mutual benefit, desire to disclose certain confidential information to one another in order to evaluate a potential business or collaborative relationship. </SPAN 6><SPAN 7>(In the capacity of disclosing information, each Party is referred to as the “Disclosing Party”, and in the capacity of receiving information, each party is referred to as the “Receiving Party”.)</SPAN 7>
<SPAN 8>NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the premises and covenants contained herein, the Parties agree as follows:</SPAN 8>
<SPAN 9>1. Purpose. </SPAN 9><SPAN 10>The Parties have entered into this Agreement to facilitate the transfer of information between them and/or one or more of their Affiliates in order for the Parties to evaluate whether or not to pursue a potential business opportunity or collaboration with respect to the development and commercialization of Prosensa’s products including, but not limited to, Drisapersen (the “Purpose”), and solely for that Purpose, the Parties have disclosed or may disclose to each other information that is proprietary and/or confidential to the Disclosing Party which it desires be treated as confidential. </SPAN 10><SPAN 11>For purposes of this Agreement, with respect to a Party, “Affiliate” shall mean a company controlled by, under the control of, or in common control with such Party.</SPAN 11>
<SPAN 12>2. Confidential Information. </SPAN 12><SPAN 13>As used herein, “Confidential Information” shall mean any and all technical and non-technical information previously, presently, or subsequently disclosed or provided by Disclosing Party and/or one or more of its Affiliates to Receiving Party and/or one or more of its Affiliates in written, oral or electronic form. </SPAN 13><SPAN 14>Confidential Information will be deemed to include, without limitation:</SPAN 14>
<SPAN 15>(a) any technology, inventions, products, chemical compounds and compositions, formulations, molecules, precursors, methods, concepts, ideas, plans, processes, specifications, characteristics, techniques, know-how and assays; clinical information such as raw data, scientific preclinical or clinical data, observations, records, databases, dosing regimes, clinical studies or protocols, posters, presentations and abstracts, product pipelines, timelines and schedules; business information such as development, marketing, sales, pricing and commercialization plans, forecasts, proposals, customer lists, suppliers, consulting relationships, operating, performance and cost structures, and any other non-public information or other trade secrets, whether scientific, clinical or financial in nature, relating directly or indirectly to the business of the Disclosing Party; and</SPAN 15>
<SPAN 16>(b) any memorandum, analysis, compilation, summary, interpretation, study, report or other document, record or material that is or has been prepared by or for the Receiving Party and that contains, reflects, interprets or is based directly or indirectly upon any information of the type referred to in Section 2(a) above;</SPAN 16>
<SPAN 17>(c) the existence and terms of this Agreement, and the fact that information of the type referred to in Section 2(a) above has been made available to the Receiving Party; and</SPAN 17>
<SPAN 18>(d) the fact that discussions or negotiations are or may be taking place with respect to a possible transaction involving the Parties, and the proposed terms of any such transaction.</SPAN 18>
<SPAN 19>3. Term. </SPAN 19><SPAN 20>The term of this Agreement commences on the Effective Date and ends on the date one (1) year thereafter. </SPAN 20><SPAN 21>Receiving Party’s obligations to protect Confidential Information disclosed under this Agreement shall survive termination of this Agreement and will be binding upon Receiving Party, its heirs, successors, and assigns for a period of five (5) years from expiration or termination of this Agreement.</SPAN 21>
<SPAN 22>4. Treatment of Confidential Information.</SPAN 22>
<SPAN 23>(a) Use; Disclosure. </SPAN 23><SPAN 24>Receiving Party shall use the Confidential Information solely for the Purpose defined above. </SPAN 24><SPAN 25>Receiving Party shall not use the Confidential Information for any other purpose, including but not limited to using it in connection with the development or commercialization of any process or product, or using it in connection with any submission to any governmental agency, including any patent office or regulatory authority, or the like, without the express written permission of Disclosing Party. </SPAN 25><SPAN 26>Receiving Party shall disseminate Confidential Information only to those employees, independent contractors, advisors, or Affiliates, on a “need to know” basis in order for Receiving Party to carry out the Purpose, and Receiving Party warrants that all such employees, independent contractors, advisors, or Affiliates shall be advised of the confidential nature of the information received and that all such employees, independent contractors, advisors, Affiliates shall be bound in writing by obligations no less stringent than the terms set forth in this Agreement. </SPAN 26><SPAN 27>Receiving Party agrees to notify Disclosing Party immediately in writing upon any loss, misuse, misappropriation, or other unauthorized disclosure of the Confidential Information of Disclosing Party that may come to Receiving Party’s attention.</SPAN 27>
<SPAN 28>(b) Degree of Care. </SPAN 28><SPAN 29>Receiving Party shall hold the Confidential Information in strict confidence, and shall take all reasonable precautions to protect the Confidential Information at all times from unauthorized disclosure, publication, or use, including, without limitation, using at least the same degree of care as it employs to protect its own Confidential Information of like nature (but in any event no less than a reasonable degree of care), acting in a manner consistent with its obligations under this Agreement.</SPAN 29>
<SPAN 30>(c) Exclusions. </SPAN 30><SPAN 31>The confidentiality, non-disclosure and non-use obligations of this Agreement shall not apply to Confidential Information disclosed to the Receiving Party that: </SPAN 31><SPAN 32>(i) can be shown by written evidence to be in the Receiving Party’s possession before receipt of the Confidential Information from Disclosing Party; </SPAN 32><SPAN 33>(ii) is independently developed by Receiving Party without the use of the Confidential Information as evidenced by written records; </SPAN 33><SPAN 34>(iii) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the Receiving Party; or </SPAN 34><SPAN 35>(iv) is rightfully received by the Receiving Party on a non-confidential basis from a third party without breach of a duty of confidentiality to Disclosing Party. </SPAN 35><SPAN 36>As used herein, the term “publicly available” shall mean readily accessible to the public in a written publication, and shall not mean information the substance of which must be pieced together from a number of different publications or other sources.</SPAN 36>
<SPAN 37>(d) Legally Required Disclosures. </SPAN 37><SPAN 38>Nothing in this Agreement shall preclude Receiving Party from making any disclosure of Confidential Information that is required by applicable law or regulation or by a valid order of a court or other governmental body having jurisdiction, provided that Receiving Party uses best efforts to limit the scope of the required disclosure, provides notification to Disclosing Party of such requirement as soon as reasonably possible, and cooperates with Disclosing Party in seeking an appropriate protective order, confidential treatment, or similar remedy limiting the subsequent use and disclosure of any information required to be disclosed.</SPAN 38>
<SPAN 39>(e) No Obligation to Proceed. </SPAN 39><SPAN 40>Nothing herein shall obligate either Party to proceed with any transaction between them, and each Party reserves the right, in its sole discretion, to terminate the discussions contemplated by this Agreement. </SPAN 40><SPAN 41>This Agreement does not constitute a binding agreement to enter into any definitive agreement. </SPAN 41><SPAN 42>Receiving Party understands that nothing herein requires the disclosure of any Confidential Information by Disclosing Party, which shall be disclosed, if at all, at the discretion of Disclosing Party.</SPAN 42>
<SPAN 43>(f) Return of Materials. </SPAN 43><SPAN 44>Immediately upon </SPAN 44><SPAN 45>(a) termination or expiration of this Agreement, </SPAN 45><SPAN 46>(b) the decision by either Party not to enter into the business or scientific relationship contemplated above, or </SPAN 46><SPAN 47>(c) a request by Disclosing Party at any time, Receiving Party will promptly turn over to Disclosing Party, or destroy, all Confidential Information of Disclosing Party and all documents, media, and other tangible materials containing any such Confidential Information and any and all extracts thereof. </SPAN 47><SPAN 48>In the event that Receiving Party destroys Confidential Information, upon the destruction thereof, Receiving Party will issue to Disclosing Party a certificate as proof of compliance with Disclosing Party’s request. </SPAN 48><SPAN 49>Notwithstanding this Section 4(f), the Receiving Party shall not be required to purge Confidential Information from its computer system’s historical back-up media, provided that such Confidential Information that is retained will remain subject to the terms of this Agreement.</SPAN 49>
<SPAN 50>(g) No Transfer or License. </SPAN 50><SPAN 51>Nothing in this Agreement is intended to grant or transfer any right to Receiving Party under any patent, copyright or other intellectual property right of Disclosing Party, nor shall this Agreement grant or transfer to the Receiving Party any right in or to the Confidential Information except as expressly set forth herein. </SPAN 51><SPAN 52>None of the Confidential Information which may be disclosed by Disclosing Party shall constitute any representation, warranty, assurance, guarantee or inducement by Disclosing Party to Receiving Party, including, without limitation, with respect to the non-infringement of intellectual property rights, or other rights of third persons.</SPAN 52>
<SPAN 53>(h) Both parties hereby acknowledges that in its review the other party’s Confidential Information it and its representatives will have access to material non-public information concerning this other party. </SPAN 53><SPAN 54>Each Party acknowledges, that it and its representatives are aware, that the United States or other applicable securities laws prohibit any person, who has received from an issuer material non-public information relating to an issuer of securities, from purchasing or selling securities of such issuer or from communicating such information to any other person under circumstances in which it is reasonably foreseeable that such person is likely to purchase or sell such securities.</SPAN 54>
<SPAN 55>5. Miscellaneous.</SPAN 55>
<SPAN 56>(a) Use of Names; Publicity. </SPAN 56><SPAN 57>Except as otherwise provided herein, nothing contained in this Agreement shall be construed as conferring any right on Receiving Party to use in any manner Disclosing Party’s name or any trade name or trademark. </SPAN 57><SPAN 58>Receiving Party will make no public announcement or other public statement concerning the existence of this Agreement or the Parties’ respective performances hereunder without the prior written consent of Disclosing Party, which may be withheld in Disclosing Party’s sole and absolute discretion, except as necessary to comply with applicable law or regulations.</SPAN 58>
<SPAN 59>(b) Assignment. </SPAN 59><SPAN 60>Receiving Party shall not transfer or assign any rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of Disclosing Party, which consent may be given or withheld in Disclosing Party’s sole and absolute discretion.</SPAN 60>
<SPAN 61>(c) Severability. </SPAN 61><SPAN 62>If any provision of this Agreement should be held invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall be unaffected and shall remain in full force and effect, to the extent consistent with the intent of the parties as evidenced by this Agreement as a whole.</SPAN 62>
<SPAN 63>(d) Waivers. </SPAN 63><SPAN 64>All waivers must be in writing and signed by the Party to be charged. </SPAN 64><SPAN 65>Any waiver or failure to enforce any provision of this Agreement on one occasion will not be deemed a waiver of any other provision or of such provision on any other occasion.</SPAN 65>
<SPAN 66>(e) Notices. </SPAN 66><SPAN 67>All notices or reports permitted or required under this Agreement will be in writing and will be sent by personal delivery or reputable expedited delivery service with signature required. </SPAN 67><SPAN 68>All such notices or reports will be deemed given upon receipt. </SPAN 68><SPAN 69>Notices will be sent to the addresses set forth at the beginning of this Agreement, in this section, or such other addresses as either Party may specify in writing.</SPAN 69>
<SPAN 70>(f) Governing Law; Jurisdiction. </SPAN 70><SPAN 71>This Agreement is made under and shall be construed according to the laws of the State of California without regard to any conflict of law principles that would provide for the application of the law of another jurisdiction. </SPAN 71><SPAN 72>Any disputes under this Agreement may be brought in the state courts and the Federal courts located in the Northern District of California, and the parties hereby consent to the personal jurisdiction and exclusive venue of these courts.</SPAN 72>
<SPAN 73>(g) Injunctive Relief. </SPAN 73><SPAN 74>Receiving Party agrees that disclosure of Confidential Information without the express written permission of Disclosing Party will cause Disclosing Party irreparable harm and that any breach or threatened breach of this Agreement by Receiving Party will entitle Disclosing Party to injunctive relief, in addition to any other legal and/or equitable remedies available to it. </SPAN 74><SPAN 75>Notwithstanding clause </SPAN 75><SPAN 76>(f), Disclosing Party may seek injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction.</SPAN 76>
<SPAN 77>(h) Independence. </SPAN 77><SPAN 78>The Parties do not intend that any agency or partnership relationship be created between them by this Agreement.</SPAN 78>
<SPAN 79>(i) Entire Agreement; Amendment. </SPAN 79><SPAN 80>This Agreement constitutes the final, complete and exclusive agreement of the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous agreements, communications, negotiations or understandings between the Parties with respect to the matters addressed herein. </SPAN 80><SPAN 81>No modification of or amendment to this Agreement will be effective unless in writing and signed by all Parties.</SPAN 81>
<SPAN 82>(j) Counterparts. </SPAN 82><SPAN 83>This Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts (including by facsimile or .pdf), each of which shall constitute an original and all of which, when taken together, shall constitute one agreement.</SPAN 83>
<SPAN 84>IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have caused this Non-Disclosure Agreement to be executed as of the Effective Date.</SPAN 84>
<SPAN 85>PROSENSA HOLDING N.V. BIOMARIN PHARMACEUTICAL INC.</SPAN 85>
